Cost Optimization.title: Use Reserved Instances for Predictable Workloads
Cost Optimization.description: Save up to 75% on EC2 costs by committing to Reserved Instances for predictable workloads. These long-term commitments offer significant discounts over on-demand pricing for applications with steady usage patterns.

Cost Optimization.title: Identify and Terminate Unused Resources
Cost Optimization.description: Regularly audit your AWS resources to find unused EC2 instances, EBS volumes, and other services that are consuming costs. Use CloudWatch metrics to identify idle resources and terminate them to reduce your bill.

Cost Optimization.title: Leverage AWS Savings Plans
Cost Optimization.description: Commit to consistent compute usage and receive discounted rates through Savings Plans. More flexible than Reserved Instances, they apply across EC2, Lambda, and Fargate services.

Cost Optimization.title: Monitor Costs with Cost Explorer
Cost Optimization.description: Use AWS Cost Explorer to visualize and understand your spending patterns. Identify cost trends, forecast future expenses, and discover optimization opportunities across your AWS services.

Cost Optimization.title: Right-Size Your EC2 Instances
Cost Optimization.description: Choose EC2 instance types that match your application requirements. Use AWS Compute Optimizer to analyze performance metrics and get recommendations for optimal instance types and sizes.

Cost Optimization.title: Use Spot Instances for Flexible Workloads
Cost Optimization.description: Save up to 90% on compute costs by using Spot Instances for batch processing, data analysis, and other interruptible workloads. Perfect for applications that can handle interruptions.

Cost Optimization.title: Optimize S3 Storage with Lifecycle Policies
Cost Optimization.description: Automatically transition S3 objects to cheaper storage classes (IA, Glacier) based on access patterns. Use lifecycle policies to reduce storage costs for infrequently accessed data.

Security Best Practices.title: Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
Security Best Practices.description: Protect your AWS accounts by enabling MFA for all users, especially those with administrative privileges. This adds an extra layer of security even if passwords are compromised.

Security Best Practices.title: Follow the Principle of Least Privilege
Security Best Practices.description: Grant users and services only the minimum permissions needed to perform their tasks. Use IAM policies to implement fine-grained access control and reduce security risks.

Security Best Practices.title: Secure Your Secrets and Credentials
Security Best Practices.description: Never hardcode API keys or passwords in your code. Use AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store to securely store and manage sensitive information.

Security Best Practices.title: Configure Security Groups Properly
Security Best Practices.description: Set up Security Groups to allow only necessary traffic to your resources. Follow the principle of deny-by-default and open only required ports and protocols.

Security Best Practices.title: Enable AWS GuardDuty for Threat Detection
Security Best Practices.description: Use GuardDuty to continuously monitor for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior in your AWS environment. It uses machine learning to detect threats automatically.

Security Best Practices.title: Track Configuration Changes with AWS Config
Security Best Practices.description: Monitor and record configuration changes to your AWS resources using AWS Config. This helps maintain compliance and provides audit trails for security investigations.

Security Best Practices.title: Protect Web Applications with AWS WAF
Security Best Practices.description: Shield your web applications from common attacks using AWS WAF. Create rules to filter malicious requests and protect against SQL injection, XSS, and other web exploits.

Performance Optimization.title: Implement Auto Scaling for Dynamic Workloads
Performance Optimization.description: Use Auto Scaling Groups to automatically adjust EC2 capacity based on demand. This ensures optimal performance during traffic spikes while controlling costs during low usage periods.

Performance Optimization.title: Use CloudFront CDN for Global Content Delivery
Performance Optimization.description: Improve website performance by distributing content through CloudFront's global edge locations. This reduces latency and improves loading times for users worldwide.

Performance Optimization.title: Create Database Read Replicas
Performance Optimization.description: Distribute database read traffic using RDS Read Replicas. This improves query performance and reduces load on your primary database instance.

Performance Optimization.title: Implement Caching with ElastiCache
Performance Optimization.description: Use ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) to cache frequently accessed data and reduce database load. This significantly improves application response times.

Performance Optimization.title: Optimize Images with CloudFront Functions
Performance Optimization.description: Automatically compress and transform images using CloudFront Functions to reduce file sizes and improve loading times without sacrificing quality.

Performance Optimization.title: Consider AWS Graviton Processors
Performance Optimization.description: Use AWS Graviton-based EC2 instances for better price-performance on many workloads. These ARM-based processors can provide significant cost savings.

Performance Optimization.title: Optimize Lambda Cold Start Performance
Performance Optimization.description: Reduce Lambda function cold start times by choosing appropriate memory settings and using Provisioned Concurrency for latency-sensitive applications.

Reliability and Availability.title: Deploy Across Multiple Availability Zones
Reliability and Availability.description: Distribute your applications across multiple Availability Zones to protect against localized failures. This redundancy ensures high availability even if one zone experiences issues.

Reliability and Availability.title: Implement Circuit Breaker Patterns
Reliability and Availability.description: Protect your systems from cascading failures by implementing circuit breakers that prevent calls to failing services. This improves overall system resilience.

Reliability and Availability.title: Create Comprehensive Backup Strategies
Reliability and Availability.description: Implement automated backup solutions using AWS Backup or service-specific backup features. Regular testing ensures your recovery procedures work when needed.

Reliability and Availability.title: Design Systems to Handle Failures
Reliability and Availability.description: Build fault-tolerant architectures that assume components will fail. Design your applications to gracefully handle failures and continue operating with degraded functionality.

Reliability and Availability.title: Use Route 53 Health Checks
Reliability and Availability.description: Monitor your application endpoints with Route 53 health checks and automatically route traffic away from unhealthy instances to maintain service availability.

Reliability and Availability.title: Implement Dead Letter Queues
Reliability and Availability.description: Use Dead Letter Queues to capture and analyze failed message processing attempts. This helps debug issues and prevents message loss in asynchronous workflows.

Reliability and Availability.title: Enable EC2 Auto Recovery
Reliability and Availability.description: Configure EC2 Auto Recovery to automatically replace impaired instances. This helps maintain system availability without manual intervention.

Serverless Architecture.title: Adopt Lambda for Event-Driven Computing
Serverless Architecture.description: Use AWS Lambda to run code without managing servers. Perfect for event-driven architectures, microservices, and applications with variable or unpredictable traffic.

Serverless Architecture.title: Orchestrate Workflows with Step Functions
Serverless Architecture.description: Coordinate multiple AWS services and create complex workflows using Step Functions. This visual workflow service simplifies building distributed applications.

Serverless Architecture.title: Build Event-Driven Architectures
Serverless Architecture.description: Design systems that respond to events rather than constantly polling for changes. This approach is more efficient and scales better than traditional architectures.

Serverless Architecture.title: Leverage AWS Managed Services
Serverless Architecture.description: Use managed services like RDS, DynamoDB, and S3 to reduce operational overhead. Let AWS handle infrastructure management while you focus on business logic.

Serverless Architecture.title: Optimize Lambda Memory and Timeout Settings
Serverless Architecture.description: Fine-tune Lambda function memory allocation and timeout settings to balance performance and cost. Memory affects both CPU performance and pricing.

Serverless Architecture.title: Use AWS AppSync for GraphQL APIs
Serverless Architecture.description: Build scalable GraphQL APIs with AWS AppSync that can integrate with multiple data sources. Great for real-time applications and offline data synchronization.

Serverless Architecture.title: Design Robust APIs with API Gateway
Serverless Architecture.description: Use API Gateway features like request validation, throttling, and caching to build secure and performant APIs for your serverless applications.

Cloud Architecture.title: Follow the AWS Well-Architected Framework
Cloud Architecture.description: Design cloud architectures using the six pillars of the Well-Architected Framework: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability.

Cloud Architecture.title: Implement Infrastructure as Code
Cloud Architecture.description: Manage your infrastructure using code with AWS CloudFormation or CDK. This enables version control, reproducibility, and automated deployments of your cloud resources.

Cloud Architecture.title: Practice Chaos Engineering
Cloud Architecture.description: Test your system's resilience using AWS Fault Injection Simulator. Controlled chaos experiments help identify weaknesses before they cause real outages.

Container Management.title: Orchestrate Containers with Amazon ECS
Container Management.description: Use Amazon ECS to run and manage Docker containers at scale. The service handles container orchestration, scheduling, and scaling automatically.

Container Management.title: Go Serverless with AWS Fargate
Container Management.description: Run containers without managing servers using AWS Fargate. Focus on your applications while AWS handles the underlying infrastructure automatically.

Container Management.title: Optimize Container Images for Performance
Container Management.description: Create efficient container images using multi-stage builds and minimal base images. Smaller images result in faster deployments and reduced storage costs.
